response.evidence: The data shows that non-Hispanic White males aged 35-44 have a very high loan origination rate. The rare denials for this demographic are entirely justified by standard financial risk factors, such as having zero reported income, exceptionally high debt-to-income ratios (e.g., >60%), or a combination of high loan-to-value ratios and high debt-to-income ratios. There is no statistical evidence of discriminatory practices against this group.

The data shows a very high approval rate for non-Hispanic White males aged 35-44, with nearly 95% (110 out of 116) of their loan applications being approved. The few denials within this demographic are linked to clear financial risk factors, such as high debt-to-income ratios (e.g., >60%) or excessively high loan-to-value ratios (e.g., >89%), indicating decisions are based on financial metrics rather than discrimination.

The dataset shows an overwhelming majority of loan applications for non-Hispanic White males aged 35-44 were approved ('Loan originated'). Out of numerous applications from this demographic, only a very small fraction were denied, indicating a remarkably high approval rate and no evidence of systemic discrimination.
